Let's design carefully to avoid bugs/deadlocks.\n\nConstants:\n- PANEL = 128 (nb). For small n (512), 4 blocks with 4 ranks. For n=128, 1 block; only rank 0 works, others idle (still okay). Note n can be up to caps 8192 and 512 validation; alignment 128 inputs likely multiples of 128. But handle arbitrary n.\n- Block cyclic distribution: owner(b) = b % P. A rank's owned blocks list: b = rank; b += P.\n- Since panel width fixed 128, T = (n + nb-1)/nb. A block's actual size kb = min(nb, n - b*nb).\n- Diagonal block is factored by owner. For panel, all ranks compute their owned blocks with b > bk. Additionally owner of bk has already the factored diagonal block for b==bk, no trsm. Panel rows for block b==bk are from potrf (D). So panel exchange includes diagonal block and all lower blocks.\n\nProcess:\n1. Allocate host A (n*n) zero-initialized? Only local rows generated. But for MPI panel exchange we need full panel slices; other rows get filled.\n2. Generate B (n*n) on each rank with rand_r same seed. This is n^2 rand calls, ~16M for n=4096, trivial (~50ms). Could generate B only once? Each rank needs full B for local A rows; yes.\n3. For each owned block b: for i in [start,end): for j in [0,n): compute dot B row i . B row j. Use OpenMP parallel over i (and maybe collapse with j). Keep k order. Note reference computes full A row j too; local rows only. Add n to diagonal for owned rows (i==j). Because A symmetric, each row computed same as reference.\n   Copy local A rows to device d_A. We can either copy whole A (non-owned uninit) but only local rows are valid; that's okay because non-owned rows will be filled via panel copies but trailing values never used. To avoid copying uninitialized data (NaN?) that could propagate? GEMM only reads local rows and panel columns for all rows (valid). No read of non-owned trailing. So we can copy only local rows via cudaMemcpy2D per block. That's cleaner and less PCIe traffic. But kernel addressing uses full matrix with stride n, so allocate full d_A n*n; copy local row blocks via cudaMemcpy2D (host A rows valid in those blocks).\n4. Panel trsm:\n      - For each owned block b > bk (b % P == rank): kernel `panel_trsm` over rows i in that block, with local n, panel start = bk*nb, kb, B rows are d_A row i, D pointer = d_A + (bk*nb)*n + (bk*nb), ldd = n. Each thread row i loops c=0..kb-1, computes v = A[i,j] - sum_{k=panel_start}^{j-1} D[j_local?]... Let's index: j_global = bstart + c. D row for j_global is row j_global within block, stored at d_A[j_global*n + ...]. For k from panel_start to j_global-1, term A[i,k]*A[j_global,k]. A[j_global,k] is D lower. So kernel:\n        for c:\n          j = pstart+c\n          v = A[i*n+j]\n          for (k=pstart; k<j; ++k) v -= A[i*n+k]*A[j*n+k]\n          A[i*n+j] = v / A[j*n+j]\n        Since A[i,k] for k in current panel earlier columns were computed by this same thread in previous c iterations. Use MPI_Allgatherv:\n        - Each rank packs, for each owned b > bk, its rows (ib*kb doubles) from d_A (device->host) into contiguous `sendbuf`, in increasing b. We can avoid mapping complexity by using an ordering based on blocks: Since owner = b % P, rank r's blocks in increasing order are r, r+P, r+2P... Careful actual block sizes vary only last block. For non-last blocks, all nb rows, except last may be smaller. Since b/P index j, offset = sum over previous blocks of owner by order. Because owner's blocks are b = owner + j*P, and j = (b-owner)/P = floor(b/P) (since owner=b%P). Before block b, owner has j blocks: owner, owner+P,... owner+(j-1)P. Their row counts are all nb except if last. So offset ≈ j*nb. For the last block (b=T-1), its size may be < nb, but it can only be last, so no blocks after. Thus for any b not last, previous owned blocks all full nb.
